problems.reason: Both state that the species is named Cuspicephalus scarfi.
Both claim the species name honors Gerald Scarfe.
Both explain the genus name derives from Latin/Greek words for cusp/pointed head.
Both refer to the formal naming/description of the genus by Martill and Etches, but with different dates.
Both state Cuspicephalus had around thirty pairs of teeth along a straight jaw section.
Both give the species name Cuspicephalus scarfi.
Both describe the significance of Cuspicephalus as expanding the known range/diversity of wukongopterids.
Mentions "previously known members were five million years older" without earlier reference to those members.
Describes the large size of Cuspicephalus as expanding the anatomical diversity of the group, focusing on the group rather than the animal itself.
